lead: Alcoholic drinks a person buys, cellars or collects — wine by colour and grape with appellation archetypes, beer by BJCP style family, whisky by country and style, other spirits, liqueurs, sake and rice wines, cider and mead, ready-to-drink, and no- and low-alcohol alternatives — with producers, breweries and distilleries in the brand register.

depts.note: Grape view first; classed appellations and icon wines are the archetypes under each grape.

b.v: regional → village → premier cru → grand cru (Burgundy); cru bourgeois → 5e–1er cru classé (Bordeaux 1855); IGT → DOC → DOCG (Italy); joven → crianza → reserva → gran reserva (Rioja)
b.w: Official appellation systems and historic classifications set the expected quality and ageing.
Weather of the harvest year and the wine's age decide whether it is ready, improving or past its best.
Domaine, château or estate standing within its appellation; recorded in the producer register.

s.brief: Each kind = one grape (varietal wine or the grape's classic appellations). Archetypes = classic appellations and icon wines, ordered originator/reference first: Burgundy grand crus (Chambertin, Romanée-Conti, Clos de Vougeot…) and NZ/Oregon Pinot under Pinot Noir; Barolo, Barbaresco under Nebbiolo; Brunello, Chianti Classico, Vino Nobile under Sangiovese; Rioja, Ribera del Duero, Vega Sicilia under Tempranillo; Hermitage, Côte-Rôtie, Penfolds Grange, Barossa Shiraz under Syrah; Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Priorat under Grenache; Napa cult Cabernet, Coonawarra under Cabernet Sauvignon; Pomerol/Masseto under Merlot; Mendoza under Malbec; Beaujolais crus under Gamay. Existing models become versions (cuvée, vintage) or are trimmed to ≈8–12 notable producers per kind. Producers go to the brand register (country, appellation, founding).

k.brief: Many Burgundy grand-cru names are already in the models: turn them into archetypes.

s.brief: Archetypes = named blend traditions and icons: Bordeaux Left Bank / Right Bank with the 1855 first growths (Lafite, Latour, Margaux, Haut-Brion, Mouton) and Saint-Émilion classification; Super Tuscans (Sassicaia, Tignanello, Ornellaia), Rhône/GSM blends, Meritage, Douro reds, Amarone-free dry blends. Dissolve the 'Other red blend' catch-all into a plain 'Red blend' kind with archetypes; trim SKU noise.

Regional and lesser-known red grapes; each kind with its home appellations as archetypes (Madiran for Tannat, Carmenère in Chile, Pinotage in Stellenbosch, Blaufränkisch in Burgenland, Plavac Mali in Dingač, Saperavi in Kakheti, Xinomavro in Naoussa). Keep the grape view; trim single-SKU models to notable producers.
